main_text.p: tius substantiæ morbum concludere possumus. Quod ad huius affectus causas antecedentes attinet, aliis omnibus medicis consentit Fernelius, sed in continente & propria ijs omnino repugnat: Etenim eodem libro de Partium morbis & Symptomatis, omnis uteri strangulatus causam proximam in venenatum vaporem his verbis refert.

Causa(inquit)accessionis hysterice[?] est va-por ex utero, non solum per venas, aut arte-rias, sed & per spiracula cæca, & latentia sublatus, atq; is certe venenatus tamq; magnus ac perniciosus, ut partium, quas at-tigerit, facultates offendat, earumq; fun-ctiones intercipiat. Si vaporis naturam spe[?]ctemus, plurimorum venenorum coditio-ne frigidus is & melancholicus. Huius focus est uterus, in quo vel mestruus sanguis, vel conclusum semen, vel alius quivis humor in hanc venenatam malignitatem corrumpitur. Hæc Fernelius, quibus libenter assentimur: sed præter illum vaporem venenatum, qui a corrupto sanguine mestruo, aut a concluso semine putrefacto ad superiora effertur, alius excitari potest minimè venenatus ab ipso utero, tempore eruptionis mesium, nimium hiante sulceptus. Huc accedit

page.notes: Printed side marks in the left margin (small quotation-type glyphs, one beside most lines from "in uenenatum" down to "uel alius") are printed marks, not text, and are not transcribed as notes. The word "spe[?]ctemus" is doubtful: the scan shows "stemus" after a line break, and the first letters are unclear. "hysterice[?]" ends in a cedilla-like sign that is uncertain. "Huc" ends the last full line; "accedit" below it is a catchword. Long s is rendered as s throughout. Words broken at line ends with a printed hyphen are kept as "va-por", "arte-rias", "at-tigerit", "fun-ctiones", "coditio-ne", "fo-cus", "supe-riora", and "pro-pria". "possumus" is split across a line end without a visible hyphen and is written whole.
